intro.title: Sam Neill
intro.description: A journey through the life, work, and characters of a New Zealand screen legend whose stories became part of our own.

entries.title: A story begins
entries.subtitle: Omagh, Northern Ireland
entries.description: Nigel John Dermot Neill was born in Omagh to Priscilla Neill, who was English, and Dermot Neill, a New Zealander serving with the Royal Irish Fusiliers.

images.alt: An early photograph of Sam Neill
images.caption: The early years

entries.title: Home in New Zealand
entries.subtitle: Christchurch, New Zealand
entries.description: At seven, he moved with his family to Christchurch. New Zealand became the place he called home and the centre of his life away from film sets.

images.alt: Christchurch and the surrounding New Zealand landscape
images.caption: Christchurch — home from the age of seven

sources.title: Exclusive: Sir Sam Neill talks deserving new knight Sir Ian Mune

entries.title: Learning the language of film
entries.subtitle: New Zealand National Film Unit
entries.description: Before international fame, Neill worked behind the camera at the National Film Unit, writing, editing, and directing documentaries. He was learning how films were built while finding his way as an actor.

images.alt: A film camera representing Sam Neill's documentary work
images.caption: Behind the camera

entries.title: Sleeping Dogs
entries.subtitle: Smith
entries.description: Roger Donaldson cast Neill as the reluctant hero of a political thriller that became a breakthrough for both men and the first New Zealand-made feature released in the United States.

images.alt: Sam Neill as Smith in Sleeping Dogs
images.caption: As Smith in Sleeping Dogs (1977)

entries.title: My Brilliant Career
entries.subtitle: Harry Beecham
entries.description: As Harry Beecham opposite Judy Davis, Neill found an international audience in Gillian Armstrong's landmark Australian film.

images.alt: Sam Neill as Harry Beecham in My Brilliant Career
images.caption: As Harry Beecham in My Brilliant Career (1979)

entries.title: Possession
entries.subtitle: Mark
entries.description: Andrzej Żuławski's feverish psychological horror asked for one of Neill's most extreme performances. The film grew into a cult landmark and revealed how fearlessly strange his choices could be.

images.alt: Sam Neill as Mark in Possession
images.caption: As Mark in Possession (1981)

sources.title: Sir Sam Neill's greatest roles: From Sleeping Dogs to Jurassic Park

entries.title: Reilly, Ace of Spies
entries.subtitle: Sidney Reilly
entries.description: Neill led the British miniseries as the elusive intelligence agent Sidney Reilly. The performance earned him the first of his three Golden Globe nominations.

images.alt: Sam Neill as Sidney Reilly in Reilly, Ace of Spies
images.caption: As Sidney Reilly in Reilly, Ace of Spies (1983)

entries.title: Two unforgettable Australian dramas
entries.subtitle: A Cry in the Dark and Dead Calm
entries.description: In consecutive years, Neill played Michael Chamberlain opposite Meryl Streep in A Cry in the Dark and John Ingram opposite Nicole Kidman in Dead Calm — two very different performances that deepened his international reputation.

images.alt: Sam Neill as Michael Chamberlain in A Cry in the Dark
images.caption: As Michael Chamberlain in A Cry in the Dark (1988)

images.alt: Sam Neill as John Ingram in Dead Calm
images.caption: With Nicole Kidman in Dead Calm (1989)

entries.title: Honoured for acting
entries.subtitle: Officer of the Order of the British Empire
entries.description: Neill was appointed an OBE for his services as an actor — formal recognition of a career that was still only gathering breadth and momentum.

images.alt: Sam Neill at a formal event
images.caption: Appointed OBE for services to acting, 1991

entries.title: Two Paddocks
entries.subtitle: Gibbston, Central Otago
entries.description: With modest ambitions, Neill planted five acres of pinot noir at Gibbston. The little vineyard grew into Two Paddocks, an organic family winery rooted across Central Otago.

images.alt: Vineyard rows at Two Paddocks in Central Otago
images.caption: Vines, animals, and home

entries.title: The Piano
entries.subtitle: Alisdair Stewart
entries.description: Jane Campion's The Piano premiered at Cannes and shared the Palme d'Or. As the controlling frontiersman Alisdair Stewart, Neill gave 1993 a dark counterpoint to the wonder that would follow.

images.alt: Sam Neill as Alisdair Stewart in The Piano
images.caption: As Alisdair Stewart in The Piano (1993)

entries.title: Welcome to Jurassic Park
entries.subtitle: Dr. Alan Grant
entries.description: Steven Spielberg's Jurassic Park made Neill's Dr. Alan Grant one of cinema's most beloved scientists — practical, sceptical, brave, and filled with wonder when it mattered.
entries.longDescription: For millions of viewers, Alan Grant became inseparable from the first sight of living dinosaurs. Neill gave the spectacle a human centre and inspired generations of childhood fascinations with fossils, fieldwork, and science.

images.alt: Sam Neill portraying Dr. Alan Grant in Jurassic Park
images.caption: As Dr. Alan Grant in Jurassic Park (1993)

sources.title: Sam Neill's greatest roles: From Sleeping Dogs to Jurassic Park

entries.title: Cinema of Unease
entries.subtitle: A personal journey through New Zealand film
entries.description: Neill returned behind the camera, co-directing with Judy Rymer a personal history of New Zealand cinema. The documentary placed the films of his homeland within the Century of Cinema series and screened at Cannes.

images.alt: Sam Neill in Cinema of Unease
images.caption: Cinema of Unease: A Personal Journey (1995)

entries.description: As the haunted designer of a vanished spacecraft, Neill helped turn Paul W. S. Anderson's science-fiction horror into an enduring cult favourite.

entries.title: Merlin
entries.subtitle: Merlin
entries.description: Neill took the title role in the television miniseries Merlin, earning another Golden Globe nomination and bringing gravity, humour, and weariness to the legendary wizard.

entries.subtitle: Jurassic Park III
entries.description: Eight years after Jurassic Park, Neill returned as Alan Grant — older, more wary, and still the person audiences trusted when everything went wrong on an island full of dinosaurs.

entries.title: Did I Ever Tell You This?
entries.subtitle: A life, written down
entries.description: After being diagnosed with stage-three angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma in 2022, Neill used a year away from acting to write his memoir. It arrived as a generous, funny collection of memories rather than what he called a cancer book.

entries.title: Good news — and a hope for others
entries.subtitle: Cancer-free after a clinical trial
entries.description: After chemotherapy stopped working, Neill joined an Australian clinical trial using CAR T-cell therapy. He announced that scans showed no cancer and used the moment to argue that more patients should have access to the treatment.

images.alt: Sam Neill in 2026
images.caption: Cancer-free after a CAR T-cell trial, April 2026

entries.title: A life that stays with us
entries.subtitle: Sydney, Australia
entries.description: Sam Neill died suddenly in Sydney at 78, surrounded by family. His whānau said he remained cancer-free and asked for privacy as they mourned an immeasurable loss. No official cause of death was disclosed in their announcement.
entries.longDescription: Across more than five decades, he moved easily between New Zealand stories, Australian cinema, European art films, Hollywood adventures, television, documentary work, writing, and wine. The performances remain — and so do the memories people made while watching them.
